## SECTION 0 — HOW TO READ THIS REPORT

**Scope & data integrity.** This analysis is built on the filed series in the pack (Sections 3–7), the company's own FY2025 results announcement [Actual], and forward-looking inputs I retrieved (rates, ERP, management guidance). Where the pack's data is unreliable, I say so and build around it. Three pack defects materially shape the method chosen:

1. **The revenue series is not continuous.** Revenue jumps from $1.784B (2017) to $4.337B (2018) with no corresponding jump in operating income — a basis change (IFRS 15 gross-up of System Fund marketing contributions and reimbursables), not a business event. Per the pack's own continuity warning I do **not** treat this as growth. Consequently, **IFRS revenue is a poor economic driver** and I do not drive the valuation off it. FY2025 evidence: IFRS revenue $5.189B contains ~$2.7B of pass-through — reportable-segment revenue was only $2.468B and fee-business revenue $1.897B [Actual, IHG FY2025 release].
2. **Capex is contested.** Pack's filed FY2025 capex is $0.028B (PP&E only); the vendor says $0.077B (includes capitalized software). I use the broader $0.077B as the owner-earnings figure (IHG is software-heavy) and test the filed figure as a sensitivity.
3. **Total-debt construction is ambiguous** (columns may overlap; SECTION 6B). I do not sum them. Instead I use IHG's own reported **net debt of $3.333B** [Actual], which is internally consistent with their 2.5x net debt/EBITDA.

**Series continuity.** Weighted-average shares fall from 235M (2015) to 154.4M (2025) — this is the real buyback program (net issuance −4.2%/yr per Section 7), not a split (pack: no split suspected). Book equity is negative ($−2.736B) — a normal consequence of sustained buybacks plus dividends exceeding retained earnings; P/B is meaningless.

- Residual-income is unusable (negative book equity). Multiples are a cross-check only (Section 8 shows the market already trades at a premium to the sell-side median).

## SECTION 0 — EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & VERDICT

**Verdict: SELL / AVOID at $159.91. No margin of safety — the price is at or above the optimistic end of every defensible valuation range.**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Base-case intrinsic value (FCFF DCF, WACC 8.5%) | **~$90 / share** |
| Probability-weighted intrinsic value | **~$97 / share** |
| Bull / market-aligned scenario | ~$146 / share |
| Bear scenario | ~$63 / share |
| Current price | $159.91 |
| Implied downside to base case | **~ −44%** |
| Implied downside to bull case | ~ −9% |
| Margin of safety at current price | **Strongly negative** |

The company is a **high-quality, asset-light, fee-based hotel franchisor** (fee margin 64.8% FY2025; ~$1.9B fee revenue) with a credible growth algorithm (high-single-digit fee growth, 100–150bps/yr margin expansion, 12–15% adjusted-EPS CAGR — all **company-stated**). The problem is not the business; it is the price. At $159.91 the market pays **~31x trailing IFRS EPS, ~18.4x forward EV/EBITDA, and ~5.0% total shareholder-yield on $1.2B of annual returns** — above even my most generous market-consistent valuation (~$146), which already assumes key money is effectively free, a 7.5% discount rate, and full algorithm delivery for five years.

The single largest analytical finding: **the pack's filed FCF ($0.870B FY2025) is materially overstated as owner earnings.** It captures only PP&E purchases ($0.028B). Management's own H1 2026 guidance is **$200–250M/yr of key money + maintenance capex and ~$350M/yr gross capex** — real cash outflows that must come out of FCF. On the correct base, true FCFF is ~$0.72B, not $0.87B. This, plus a market discount rate (~8.5% WACC) rather than a bond-proxy rate, is why intrinsic value sits well below the tape.

---

## SECTION 1 — IDENTITY, BUSINESS & DATA-QUALITY AUDIT

**Business.** IHG is the world's third-largest hotel group (~1.03M rooms, ~6,963 hotels, 21 brands, ~160M loyalty members) behind Marriott and Hilton [Actual — FY2025 6-K; research brief]. The economic engine is **fee income — franchise and management fees** — $1,897M in FY2025 (76.9% of reportable-segment revenue), plus 17 owned/leased hotels and pass-through System Fund reimbursables that inflate total IFRS revenue to $5,189M. This fee model produces a 64.8% fee margin and requires minimal capital beyond **key money** (cash paid to owners to secure long-term contracts) and software.

**Data-quality audit — items I will not treat as business events:**

1. **2018 revenue discontinuity ($1.784B → $4.337B, +143%).** Basis change (IFRS 15 adoption grossing up System Fund reimbursables and owned/leased hotel revenue). The pack's own Section 0 continuity warning applies. **The trailing-5-year revenue CAGR of +16.7% (Section 7) is a COVID-recovery artifact, not a growth rate** — I reject it as a forecast input.
2. **2015 operating income $1.499B / net income $1.224B** are anomalous vs. the 2016–17 level (~$0.71–0.74B / ~$0.46–0.54B) and exceed every later year. Non-representative basis/one-off. **Excluded from all trend work.**
3. **Capex definitional failure (Section 5/6):** filed $0.028B (PP&E only) vs. vendor $0.077B (adds capitalized software) vs. **management guidance $200–250M/yr key money + maintenance, ~$350M/yr gross** [Actual — H1 2026 call]. The pack's `FCF` column (OCF − $0.028B) is overstated. I use management's number. This is the most consequential judgment in the analysis.

## SECTION 12 — FORECAST & VALUATION

### 12.1 Valuation engine selection

**Engine: 10-year explicit FCFF discounted at WACC, with terminal growth 2.5%, audited across scenarios using a 2-stage DCF.**

**Why FCFF, not FCFE:** IHG's net debt is material ($3.33B), and leverage is managed dynamically through buybacks (debt is recycled into fewer shares), so equity-cash-flow attribution to shareholders is complex. FCFF values the whole enterprise and subtracts debt — cleaner.

**Why 10-year, not 5-year:** The growth algorithm (12–15% adjusted EPS CAGR) is "medium to long term" per management — a period far beyond one year. A 10-year explicit path with declining growth lets the algorithm play out honestly and avoids over-relying on terminal value.

**Why not a single-year multiple:** The pack itself warns against reducing the company to a trailing number. IHG's fee margin is expanding structurally (61.2% → 64.8% → 65.9% H1'26), its pipeline converts to rooms over 2–3 years, and the buyback is accretive. These dynamics require a multi-year path.
